title: policy
description: A gate on a way in. A trigger names one or more policies; each fires a domain port operation the way a trigger's `fire` does, reading what the kind and the guarding plugin hand as context.* (the principal, the session, a challenge). The graph behind it allows by answering, and refuses with a reason where it does not; `outcomes` says what each reason means: deny, or challenge the caller. A policy never validates a credential -- the guard has done that before any policy runs -- it decides what a verified (or absent) identity may do.

$schema.description: The kind of this document: its published schema URL, or the alias @wilanis/policy.schema.json.

description.description: What this policy decides, in one or two sentences.

label.description: A short human name for this document, shown wherever a reader sees it instead of its path. Absent: the file name stands in.

decide.description: The decision: one run node. `run` names a domain port operation (path#operation) and `in` gives every value it takes, reading {{context.*}} -- context.principal, context.session, context.challenge from the guard, and whatever the kind hands. A read that may be missing (an anonymous caller has no principal) feeds an input the operation declares optional.

description.description: What the decision reads and asks, for a reader of the policy.

label.description: A short human name for this decision, shown wherever a reader sees it.

outcomes.description: reason -> what it means. Every reason the decision can refuse with is a key here, and every key is a reason it reaches (A002, A003). `deny` ends the run; `challenge` asks the guard to open a challenge of `method` and tells the caller how to answer it. Allowing is the decision answering, so it is never written.

effect.description: What this reason does: deny ends the run; challenge asks the guard to open a challenge and tells the caller how to answer it.

method.description: challenge only: the method the guard opens, one its settings declare (otp).

description.description: What this reason means, shown to whoever is refused.

proves.description: context.* paths that are present once this policy allows -- context.principal, context.session for a policy that denies anonymous callers. A resolver declared required may lean on it (A006): the trigger the resolver is read under names this policy, so the read never finds nothing.
